item.title: A STEM-humanities faultline in IITs may have been exposed by Sahil death
item.description: Sahil Wakode’s death by suicide has sparked significant discussions about academic culture at IIT-B. The event has illustrated the divide between students in STEM and those in humanities. While some students view incidents through procedural lenses, others focus on social identities and power dynamics. The protests that followed reflected this differing perspective, highlighting underlying tensions on campus.
item.dc:creator: HEMALI CHHAPIA

item.title: Bihar: After Jamui, Samastipur, another girl harassed in public at tourist site
item.description: A video reportedly showing a minor girl being harassed in Banka has emerged online. Following this incident, police registered a case against six unidentified youths for their actions. The video appears to have been recorded six months ago at Mandar Parvat tourist site, according to initial investigations. Similar incidents in Samastipur and Muzaffarpur have previously led to multiple arrests.

item.title: Microsoft shakes up communications team; CEO Satya Nadella sends memo to employees
item.description: Microsoft is shifting its communications strategy to enhance the roles of its employees in public messaging. The company will move its communications team under Brad Smith's organization, focusing on legal and public affairs. Satya Nadella emphasized the importance of employees who are closer to products in telling Microsoft's story. Frank Shaw, the longtime communications chief, will transition to an advisory role as part of this restructuring.

item.title: Meet Vishvavardhan Sharma, 9, who built an offline Gita app
item.description: Introducing Vrishvardhan Sharma, a gifted nine-year-old from Bengaluru whose early mastery of the Bhagavad Gita has brought him into the national spotlight. He completed many Gita parayanas and memorized Panini’s Ashtadhyayi, showcasing his dedication. Beyond academic pursuits, he ventured into programming, creating impactful apps such as GitaVardhan and KannadaVardhan to connect people with ancient wisdom. His unique ability to merge age-old scholarship with contemporary innovation has garnered him various honors.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: ‘Kashmiri Pandits driven out by Pakistan-backed terrorists’: India at UN
item.description: In response to Pakistan's statements at the UN Human Rights Council about Kashmir, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi asserted that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India. He denounced Pakistan's occupation of the territory while drawing attention to the systematic violence faced by religious minorities in Pakistan. Furthermore, Randhir Jaiswal dismissed Pakistan's assertions about the Indus Waters Treaty, reinforcing India's steadfast stance amid ongoing bilateral tensions.
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: ‘Lives may be sacrificed’: Saudi Grand Mufti urges troops to fight against Houthis
item.description: In a rallying call, Saudi Arabia's Grand Mufti has urged border troops to gear up for crucial sacrifices in the fight against the Houthi movement. He highlighted the necessity of reinstating Yemen's Saudi-backed administration amid escalating hostilities. Recent weeks have seen intensified assaults from both sides, with missile strikes increasingly threatening Saudi territory, as the Houthis target vital infrastructure and cities.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: From Russia to India: Meet Yury Lisichko, the man fixing shooters' pistol grips
item.description: Russian pistol coach Yury Lisichko arrived in India in 2009 for a one-year assignment with the Indian Army. Years later, his Greater Noida workshop has become a stop for shooters seeking the right pistol grip. From Anish Bhanwala and Manu Bhaker to Jitu Rai and Sarabjot Singh, shooters have worked with Lisichko, who studies their hands, modifies fresh pieces of wood and keeps adjusting until the pistol and shooter work together.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Massachusetts turns retired cranberry bog into habitat for rare brook trout
item.description: Massachusetts is restoring Century Bog, a former cranberry farm in Plymouth and Wareham, to complete protection of Red Brook from White Island Pond to Buttermilk Bay. The restored wetland and stream channel could benefit about 60 conservation-priority species, including “salter” brook trout that move between freshwater and saltwater estuaries.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Intel cuts VP ranks from 450 to 200; CFO says ‘cultural problem’ delayed products
item.description: Intel has cut its vice president ranks from about 450 to 200 and halved management layers from 12 to six under CEO Lip-Bu Tan. CFO David Zinsner blamed a cultural problem of veto power and poor transparency for years of slow execution and delayed products. He said Intel 18A yields are ahead of schedule, 14A risk production is set for 2027, and gross margins have climbed into the low 40s.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Man says working in ‘incognito mode’ helped him get promoted; shares tips
item.description: Harshit Mahawar claims that using incognito mode for office work has produced unexpected professional benefits. He believes it prevents employers from monitoring his browsing activity while working. Mahawar states he received better salary hikes and promotions as a result of this habit. He became the youngest employee to rise from a fresher to vice president in three years. However, there is no evidence that incognito mode directly influences career advancement.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Delhi’s old high-rises face mandatory structural safety audits under new DDA order
item.description: Delhi Development Authority has directed owners of older high-rise buildings to complete structural safety audits within three months. This directive applies to buildings sanctioned before March 21, 2001, with high footfall also included. Recent building collapses in Delhi have raised concerns about structural integrity and safety. The audit aims to assess the earthquake resistance of these buildings. Failure to comply may result in action against the owners.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: PVR Inox ordered to pay Rs 6,000 after movie show cancelled 10 minutes after start
item.description: A consumer complaint was upheld by the Hyderabad district commission regarding a cancelled film show. The complainant experienced distress due to the abrupt cancellation of the movie after 10 minutes. The theatre management initially attributed the cancellation to low occupancy, and later to a technical issue. The commission found insufficient evidence supporting the theatre's claims for the show cancellation.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex opens over 100 points up, NSE Nifty50 trades above 23,000
item.description: Dalal Street began trading on a positive note after experiencing a significant decline earlier this week. BSE Sensex opened over 100 points higher, while NSE Nifty traded above 23,000. However, rising crude oil prices are impacting overall market sentiment and limiting gains. Foreign investors have also contributed to the decline by selling Indian shares worth over 50 billion rupees.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: 'Let's race, not wrestle': 5 takeaways as Trump-Xi navigate trade, Taiwan and AI
item.description: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met at the White House to discuss key issues like trade and artificial intelligence. They agreed to extend their trade truce by two months while significant disputes remain unresolved. Taiwan and its security implications were also central to the discussions, as Xi urged caution regarding the island. Both leaders emphasized the importance of avoiding confrontation and fostering cooperation between their countries.
item.dc:creator: VIVEK DUBEY

item.title: Vanderbilt's $5-an-acre sale in 1914 became Pisgah National Forest in 1916
item.description: In 1914, Edith Vanderbilt made a landmark decision by selling 86,700 acres of land to the federal government for conservation purposes, significantly below market value. This generous act was aimed at promoting her late husband's vision of preserving essential forests. The area ultimately became Pisgah National Forest in 1916, laying the groundwork for ecological protection and setting a visionary example for public land conservation in the eastern U.S.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Wyoming storage shed turns out to be 140-year-old Chinese laundry
item.description: A weathered Wyoming cabin used as a storage shed for decades turned out to be a 140-year-old Chinese laundry and bathhouse owned by Sam Sing. After an eight-year effort, the historic building has been moved to a museum, where it will be restored and used to tell the story of Lander’s early Chinese community.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: "I complained and had to resign": Employee on cost of reporting harassment
item.description: In a powerful recount, Ritica detailed her decision to resign after encountering workplace harassment, met with inadequate responses from management. Despite reporting the incidents to HR, her cries for help were dismissed, leading to even more obstacles, including pressure toward her coworkers to file complaints against her. Ultimately, she felt compelled to leave, convinced that the situation would remain unchanged.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Rajinikanth’s ‘Baashha’ idea was born from a scene discussed during ‘Hum’ shoot
item.description: The iconic film 'Baashha', starring Rajinikanth, was born from a casual chat on the set of 'Hum' involving Amitabh Bachchan and Govinda. They brainstormed a police scene that never made it to the final cut. Inspired, Rajinikanth relayed this to director Suresh Krissna during 'Annamalai'. With their title in hand, they crafted 'Baashha', completing it in a mere five to six months.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Man's $899K bet on Nantucket cliff cottage: Still standing 5 years later
item.description: Massachusetts car dealer Charles Fotopoulos bought a 1951 Nantucket cottage for $899,000 in 2021, knowing coastal erosion posed a serious risk. He said he would be satisfied if the property lasted five years. Five years later, the home remains standing, but only a few feet separate it from a 40-foot drop to the beach below, as erosion continues.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu's Class 10 marksheet resurfaces: actress scored 887/1000 marks
item.description: Samantha Ruth Prabhu and her husband Raj Nidimoru are thrilled to welcome their first child soon. Alongside this joyous news, a nostalgic Class 10 report card showcasing her academic excellence has emerged online. With her pregnancy announcement, Samantha humorously reflected on her former scholastic achievements. As she embarks on the journey of motherhood, she seems poised to take a step back from her film endeavors.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Vedaant: Famous surname brings pressure, but I want my own identity in swimming
item.description: As the son of celebrated actor R. Madhavan, Vedaant Madhavan gears up for the 2026 Asian Games, aiming to carve out his niche in the swimming world. Prioritizing the 200m freestyle over his usual long-distance events, Vedaant is committed to training hard. Despite facing the pressures of his lineage, he remains intensely focused, embodying the spirit of discipline and perseverance on this competitive journey.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Iran gives US six days to meet conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz: Report
item.description: Iran has granted the United States a six-day window to address its conditions for re-establishing access to the Strait of Hormuz. Key points include the lifting of U.S. sanctions on Iranian ports and the release of frozen Iranian funds. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has engaged with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi amid rising tensions.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: ‘It is unholy, it is illegal’: Iran President Pezeshkian denies nuclear bomb ambition
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has reiterated the peaceful intent of the country's nuclear program, emphasizing that it is not designed for weapon development. He expressed Iran's willingness to cooperate with international inspections and reduce its stockpile of enriched uranium. Pezeshkian pointed to the US's preference for military action over diplomatic solutions as a key factor in escalating tensions, asserting that Iran's military stance is purely defensive.

item.title: Oil slips 1% as traders hope for US-Iran truce amid fresh attacks on Saudi pipeline
item.description: Following a tumultuous week influenced by geopolitical unrest and supply worries, oil prices have dipped slightly. WTI crude now stands at $93.52 a barrel, while Brent crude has retreated to $105.80. Ongoing negotiations aim to address the Middle East conflict, which has considerably strained energy supplies. In Saudi Arabia, military operations have further heightened supply concerns, underscoring the persistent instability in the region impacting global oil markets.

item.title: Fed up, you are adding to court’s burden: HC to Election Commission on symbol row
item.description: Calcutta High Court expressed frustration at the Election Commission for assigning the 'envelope' symbol to a different party. The Indian Secular Front, which won a previous election using this symbol, is now at a disadvantage. Justice Krishna Rao questioned the commission's impartiality and decisions leading to legal disputes. The ISF's counsel argued that voters would be confused with this allocation during the bypolls.

item.title: US tightens visa rules on ‘birth tourism’: What Indian travellers need to know
item.description: The United States has introduced stricter visa regulations aimed at curbing commercial birth tourism. Targeting those involved in these networks, the State Department highlights that seeking US citizenship through childbirth is not a legitimate basis for visitor visas. However, pregnant travelers visiting for valid purposes, like medical care, are not outright prohibited. Transparency during the visa process is crucial for all applicants.

item.title: After seven months away, Akash Deep's 'ubad-khabad' journey reaches comeback point
item.description: Akash Deep has seen it all. Rejection, loss, sacrifice, fame and success—but the darkest chapter of his life came when his elder sister was diagnosed with cancer last year. Then he suffered a lower-stress fracture, which kept him out of action for seven months. The Indian pacer is now back, reflecting on the people and moments that shaped him, the risks he took for Bengal and his hunger to return to India colours.
item.dc:creator: PRATYUSH RAJ

item.title: Meet Terry Fox: He lost his leg to cancer, then ran 5,373 km across Canada
item.description: Terry Fox began his Marathon of Hope on April 12, 1980, running across Canada for cancer awareness. He trained for months, covering over 5,000 kilometres before starting his journey. Fox ran daily through various weather conditions, reaching communities to discuss cancer research. Unfortunately, on September 1, 1980, he had to stop running as his cancer spread to his lungs.
item.dc:creator: TIMESOFINDIA.COM

item.title: ‘Jaldi kar, Panvel nikalna hai’: Comedy show turns ugly at an Ahmedabad university
item.description: During a comedy event at Nirma University, a student's remark led to a confrontation with a professor. The professor allegedly grabbed the student's collar and issued a threat in response. The National Students' Union of India demanded an apology from the professor and called for an impartial inquiry into the incident. The university has not yet publicly responded to these demands or commented on the incident.
item.dc:creator: HADI KHAN
